data.message: Merge branch 'fix/cobot-pump-moveit-tip-link'

data.author: Kamal Mohy El Dine
data.message:
fix: tip the MoveIt planning chain at the cobot pump's tcp

The arm group's chain tipped at hand_tcp for the franka hand and at link8 for
everything else, so the two supported end effectors disagreed about what a pose
goal means. With a pump mounted, a goal named the flange while the pump's own
tcp frame, 105 mm further along z, was present in the URDF but unreachable as a
planning target. Planning to the tool is the reason that frame exists.

Resolve the tip from the mounted end effector instead, keeping the flange for
ids that declare no tcp of their own and for hand:=false, so no unknown ee_id
can name a link the URDF lacks.

Add regression tests pinning the chain tip to the tcp link the URDF places for
the mounted end effector, and pinning the flange when nothing is mounted. The
first fails on the ten cobot pump variants before this change.

Verified by generating every arm, end effector, prefix and hand combination (61
SRDFs) before and after: byte-identical except the ten cobot pump variants that
carry a hand, whose only changed line is the chain tip. Loading the result
through MoveIt's own parser gives a valid seven joint chain whose ready-pose tip
sits 105 mm below the previous one.

MIGRATION: pose goals for ee_id:=cobot_pump shift by 105 mm along the flange z
axis. Setups that added that offset themselves must drop it.

Signed-off-by: Kamal Mohy El Dine <kamal.mohy@franka.de>

data.author: Kamal Mohy El Dine
data.message:
fix: apply no_prefix to the end effector as well as the arm

franka_arm dropped the prefix from its link names under no_prefix but
franka_robot still attached the end effector to <robot_type>_link8 and let
the end effector prefix itself, so the two halves of the robot stopped
referring to each other: every no_prefix description carrying an end
effector named a parent link the urdf did not define and was rejected by
the urdf parser, while the srdf, which does honour no_prefix, named end
effector links the urdf did not have.

franka_hand already declared a no_prefix parameter it never read, so this
wires up what was intended rather than introducing a new concept.

The macro's own default was the quoted string 'false', which is truthy in
python; it has to be a real boolean now that it decides the link prefix,
otherwise direct callers of the macro would silently lose it.

On main 20 of the 116 generated urdf variants fail check_urdf, all of them
no_prefix combined with an end effector. All 116 pass here, and the only
generated output that changes is those 20 previously unloadable ones.

Signed-off-by: Kamal Mohy El Dine <kamal.mohy@franka.de>

data.author: Kamal Mohy El Dine
data.message:
docu: state that the fer model is not supported

The tooling still offers fer as an accepted robot_model in create_urdf.py and in
the visualization launch arguments, with nothing anywhere saying it is
unsupported. Users reasonably read that as a maintained model and report defects
in its data, which we do not intend to fix.

Record the support status in the README together with the two concrete
inconsistencies that prompt those reports: one inertia tensor is not physically
realisable, and the link masses do not sum to the product manual total. Point
readers at fr3/fp3, which are equivalent kinematically and dynamically.

The model itself is untouched and still generates.

Context: https://github.com/frankarobotics/franka_description/issues/23

Signed-off-by: Kamal Mohy El Dine <kamal.mohy@franka.de>

data.author: Kamal Mohy El Dine
data.message:
fix: default the tcp offset to the mounted end effector's own value

The tcp offset is a property of the end effector, but it was specified in two
places that disagreed with it. The franka_robot macro declared tcp_xyz:='0 0 0',
while every robot entry point declared '0 0 0.1034'. The offset therefore
survived only because the entry point passed it back down, and two defects
followed from that.

Calling the franka_robot macro directly without tcp_xyz - which downstream
packages and user xacros do - silently produced hand_tcp coincident with the
mounting frame, reported as issue #31 on GitHub. Separately, the entry points
hardcoded the franka hand's 0.1034 for every end effector, so a robot built with
ee_id:=cobot_pump placed the pump tcp 1.6 mm short of the 0 0 0.105 the pump
itself declares.

Make an unspecified tcp_xyz resolve to the end effector's own offset, and drop
the hardcoded value from the entry points so the resolution is what decides. An
explicitly passed tcp_xyz still wins everywhere.

Add regression tests pinning the resolved offset to what the end effector
produces standalone, exercised through both the entry points and a direct macro
call, plus one asserting an explicit override still takes precedence. All three
fail before this change.

Verified by generating every robot, end effector, self-collision, prefix and
override combination (50 descriptions) before and after: output is
byte-identical except for the ten cobot pump variants, which gain the corrected
offset. check_urdf passes on all of them.

Reported in https://github.com/frankarobotics/franka_description/issues/31

Signed-off-by: Kamal Mohy El Dine <kamal.mohy@franka.de>

data.author: Kamal Mohy El Dine
data.message:
fix: build the dev container when the host UID/GID already exists

scripts/create_urdf.sh and scripts/visualize_franka.sh pass --build-arg
USER_UID=$(id -u) --build-arg USER_GID=$(id -g). The base image
osrf/ros:jazzy-desktop already contains an "ubuntu" user and group at 1000:1000,
so groupadd aborts with "GID '1000' already exists" for any host account holding
a colliding id, which on a stock Ubuntu install is the first user. Both helper
scripts then fail before doing any work.

Create the group and user only when the id is still free, and refer to the
account as UID:GID afterwards so the rest of the file does not depend on the
name it ended up with. Docker resolves HOME from /etc/passwd for a numeric USER,
so ~/.bashrc still lands in the right home directory either way.

Verified against osrf/ros:jazzy-desktop for 1000:1000, 1000:100 and 1001:1001:
all three now build, /workspaces is writable, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is correct and
xacro is on PATH. Before the change the first two failed in groupadd.

Ported from the community contributions
https://github.com/frankarobotics/franka_description/pull/9 (approach) and
https://github.com/frankarobotics/franka_description/pull/29 (login shell),
reported in https://github.com/frankarobotics/franka_description/issues/28

Co-authored-by: Uli Köhler <ukoehler@techoverflow.net>
Co-authored-by: Arnaud TANGUY <arn.tanguy@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Kamal Mohy El Dine <kamal.mohy@franka.de>

data.author: Rafael Papallas
data.message:
Added avoid collision when pump is used as ee.

The arm SRDF only emitted end-effector disable_collisions rules for the
franka_hand, so a robot configured with ee_id:=cobot_pump produced an SRDF in
which the pump link sits in permanent collision with link7 and link8. MoveIt
consequently rejects every state of such a robot as colliding.

Submitted upstream as
https://github.com/frankarobotics/franka_description/pull/30

Signed-off-by: Kamal Mohy El Dine <kamal.mohy@franka.de>

data.author: kuhn_an
data.message:
refactor: Remove gazebo tags/macros/args from franka_description

Make the description package simulator-agnostic. All gazebo SDF and
transmission machinery, the gazebo world anchor, and the gazebo-specific
self-collision suppression are removed; the gazebo:=false argument and the
gazebo_ros export are dropped throughout robots, end_effectors and the URDF
generation workflow.

Self-collision geometry is now gated by the include_self_collision_geometry
capability flag instead of a gazebo toggle. The removed gazebo content is
relocated to franka_gazebo, which owns the simulator-specific blocks.

The removal of the public gazebo xacro argument is recorded in a CHANGELOG
UNRELEASED migration note: consumers that passed gazebo:=true must now use
the franka_gazebo bringup entry points; the old argument is inert.

Behavior-preserving: URDF expansions are byte-identical to before.

data.author: kuhn_an
data.message:
fix: define modified_prefix in tmrv0_2 description for mobile_teleop

The shared bringup franka_arm.urdf.xacro passes arm_prefix="${modified_prefix}"
to the franka_arm_ros2_control macro, but tmrv0_2.urdf.xacro was the only
robot description not defining the file-scope modified_prefix property. As a
result mobile_teleop.launch.py (robot_type: tmrv0_2) failed with
'name 'modified_prefix' is not defined'.

Add the arm_prefix arg plus prefix/modified_prefix properties to match the
established arm-description pattern; the mobile base links are intentionally
left unprefixed.
